section_summary: John H. Schlosser clarifies that the Greenville College Student Association did not criticize the President for declining to invoke the Neutrality Act in the conflict involving Japan. He argues that existing neutrality legislation inadvertently favors an industrialized aggressor able to import American raw materials, and urges measures to restrict war-material exports to Japan. He also welcomes a firmer U.S. foreign policy and the extension of monetary credits to China.

subfiles.title: Letter clarifying the Greenville College Student Association’s position on exports of war materials to Japan
subfiles.from: John H. Schlosser, President of the Student Association of Greenville College
subfiles.about: Schlosser explains the Student Association’s call for measures limiting American exports of war materials to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Schlosser says the Greenville College student association did not object to the President's decision not to invoke the Neutrality Act, but argues it benefits an industrialized aggressor; supports discriminatory embargoes and credits to China.
